summary: An invite becomes an account of the kind the invite names: a vault owner sets up a vault in the browser before anything is sent, an administrator runs the identical derivation and discards the Master Key, and one transaction writes the principal, its password credential, a wrapper and profile record where they apply, and the invite's consumption.

read.role: the rule by which registration starts its session, and the idle lock and pagehide lock that bind the keys a new vault holds while it waits to be read
the first read and decryption of the vault that a failed first read repeats in place

sections: Bootstrap: the first administrator, and the locked-out one
read.role: the invite row this consumes, its kind, and the generic refusal every bad invite shares
the validator the profile record is written through, and the GET /api/records the first read of a new vault calls
the payload shape whose two required keys registration writes
the kind: currency rows that are the whole of the main-currency list
the schema this writes into, the headers the page is served with, and the Public group that GET /register and POST /api/register belong to, which the gate passes with no session

the form, input and progress conventions, including the Input's message line, its hint and error forms, and its ARIA wiring, the phone-width sizes, and the fact that the unauthenticated screens sit outside the shell
the two forms the invite's kind chooses between, the username field and its message line, every refusal state, and the card shown when the first read of a new vault fails
the unlock card a lock draws over a new vault that is waiting to be read, which asks for the password only

page.value: GET /register?invite=<token>, server-rendered Jinja, embedding the server's current default KDF envelope and, for a vault owner invite, the currency half of the symbol table. An invalid token renders an error page with no form

formIsChosenByTheInvite.value: the rendered form is the one the invite's kind calls for. An administrator invite renders no currency picker and states on the page that this link creates an administrator account with no vault. Nothing on either form lets the person choose the kind

endpoint.value: POST /api/register with invite token, username, Auth Key, salt and KDF parameter envelope, plus, for a vault owner, wrapped DEK and its nonce and the profile record's id, schema version, ciphertext and nonce

payloadIsCheckedAgainstTheInvite.value: the invite row's kind is the discriminator. A payload carrying a wrapper or a profile record against an administrator invite is a Bad Request, and one omitting them against a vault owner invite is too. Nothing in the request names a kind

kdfParameters.value: Argon2id at 64 MiB memory, 3 iterations, parallelism 1, over a 128-bit salt, via the argon2id library (npm argon2id, from openpgpjs), HKDF-split into Master Key and Auth Key

saltSize.value: a random 128-bit salt from crypto.getRandomValues, validated server-side as exactly 16 bytes

dekSize.value: a random 256-bit DEK, wrapped under the Master Key with AES-256-GCM

administratorDerivation.value: the same salt generation, the same Argon2id at the same parameters, and the same HKDF split, after which the Master Key is discarded. No DEK, no wrapper, no profile record, no main currency

initialProfilePayload.value: { mainCurrency, createdAt }, the two required keys of the profile payload. The optional ones are written later by the settings that own them

profileAad.value: account_id empty, record_type profile, its own record_id, its own schema_version, version 1, built entirely before the request is sent because principal_id is not part of the AAD

tablesWritten.value: principals takes identity and kind only, meaning the normalized username, the kind copied from the invite, and the two timestamps, and no key column. credentials takes exactly one row with method 'password' for both kinds, its params holding the request's salt and KDF envelope verbatim and its verifier the Argon2id hash of the submitted Auth Key. dek_wrappers takes exactly one row for a vault owner and none at all for an administrator

onePasswordCredential.value: enforced by a unique index on principal_id restricted to method = 'password', written in the same transaction as the principal row

methodIsNotClientInput.value: the server writes 'password' and no endpoint in v1 accepts any other value, so a payload carrying a method field is a Bad Request

kindIsNotClientInput.value: the server copies kind from the invite row and no endpoint anywhere writes it again. A payload carrying a kind field of any value is rejected

registrationSession.value: the session starts by the same rule as a sign-in. The account is new, so the carried session is at most another account's, and a live one is deleted and replaced. A failed registration leaves the carried session working

oneTransaction.value: the principal row, its password credential row, its wrapper and profile record where they apply, and the invite's consumption commit together or not at all

passwordPolicy.value: at least 12 characters and a zxcvbn score of at least 3, no composition rules. Client-enforced by construction, because the server never sees the password

noRecoveryAcknowledgement.value: the screen states plainly that there is no password recovery and requires an explicit acknowledgement before submitting. The administrator form carries none and claims nothing about recovery in its place

usernameRules.value: normalized by trimming and lowercasing before storage and comparison, 3 to 32 characters of [a-z0-9._-], unique across one namespace covering both kinds. The reserved sentinel system:bootstrap is refused as a username, since a colon is outside the set

usernameRuleIsOneRuleInTwoPlaces.value: the browser and the server apply the same rule, held in tests/fixtures/usernames.json as {"accept": [{"raw", "normalized"}], "refuse": [raw]}. Whitespace in it is ASCII space and tab only. pytest runs every case through the server's normalization and the client tests run every case through the browser's check, and both must agree with the file. Coverage: 3 and 32 characters, 2 and 33, each of . _ -, uppercase, leading and trailing whitespace, an inner space, a character outside the set, a non-ASCII letter, the empty string, system:bootstrap

usernameFieldBehaviour.value: the submit button stays disabled until the trimmed username fits, on both forms, and Enter in any field derives and sends nothing while it is disabled. The request carries the value the browser checked. The field lowercases as typed, has no maxlength, and carries autocapitalize="none", autocorrect="off", spellcheck="false" and autocomplete="username". The message line is the hint until the value is wrong, and its error timing (character outside the set and a 33rd character on typing, 1 or 2 characters on blur, empty keeps the hint, clears while typing) and exact copy are in the screen file. The input names the line in aria-describedby, carries aria-invalid="true" while it is an error, and the line is a polite live region

serverValidation.value: salt exactly 16 bytes, KDF envelope parameters at or above the server's configured minimum, and wrapped DEK and profile blobs within the blob and quota limits

mainCurrencyList.value: exactly the kind: currency rows of the operator's symbol table, seeded from the FX provider's own currency list. Not the full ISO 4217 set

mainCurrencyStorage.value: only inside the encrypted profile record, never as a plaintext column

checkOrder.value: POST /api/register answers the first check that fails, in this order: 1 body shape (JSON object, known fields only, each of its type, so kind, method and unknown fields fail here), 2 the username against the rule, 3 the rest of the input (salt, KDF envelope, and where present dekNonce as 96 bits of base64 and wrappedDek as base64), 4 the invite (pending, unexpired), 5 the payload against the invite's kind, 6 the username is free across both kinds, 7 the profile record through the record validator. Steps 1 to 3 read only the request, so they cost no database read

refusalAnswers.value: step 2: Bad Request with body {"refused":"username"}. Step 4: Bad Request with body {"refused":"invite"}, byte-identical in status, headers and body whether the token is unknown, empty, used, expired or revoked. Step 6: Conflict, the same whichever kind holds the name. Steps 1, 3 and 5: Bad Request with no refused member. Step 7: the record validator's own answer, with no refused member. Status names map to numbers only in the cited table (400, 409)

refusedMemberRule.value: a Bad Request carries {"refused":"<reason>"} only where a feature file pins that reason and only when it tells the caller nothing it did not send or could not already learn. Every other Bad Request carries no refused member

everyRefusalWritesNothing.value: every refusal, Conflict included, and a Server Error raised inside the transaction, writes nothing and leaves the invite pending, because the checks and the writes share the one transaction

browserAnswerMapping.value: the browser reads refused from a JSON body. A body that is not JSON or has no refused member is a general refusal. refused username shows the username field's rule error, refused invite the invalid-invite card, Conflict the taken message, any other refusal status the nothing-was-created message, and no response, a Server Error or any status of that class from a proxy the did-not-go-through message. Every answer but the invite's leaves every field filled. Copy is in the screen file

serverRefusalOfUsernameIsDrift.value: a {"refused":"username"} reaching the browser means the two copies of the rule have drifted, which the shared fixture prevents. The screen shows the server-refused-username message with the hint's rule, and editing the username returns the line to the hint

enumerationIsAcceptedHere.value: a taken username is reported clearly. Username enumeration at registration is accepted rather than defended, because the endpoint is invite-gated. The invite check and the kind check come before the taken check, so only a request the invite would accept learns whether a username exists. The refusal is the same whichever kind holds the name, so the attempt reveals existence but not kind

noWeakFallback.value: a client that cannot run WASM Argon2id fails hard with no weaker fallback KDF, for both kinds. A client that can run WASM but cannot allocate the KDF's memory gets a distinct hard failure naming the moment rather than the device, with a retry and no vault created, and must not fall back to weaker parameters

derivationRunsInAWorker.value: run derivation in a Web Worker so the UI thread stays responsive, with a busy state

firstReadFailureStands.value: when the first GET /api/records after a successful POST /api/register fails, the registration stands: the account exists and its session is live. The client keeps the Master Key, DEK and wrapper in the same document, starts the idle timer and offers to read again. There is no page load and no password prompt, because a load drops the keys and asks for the password just chosen

firstReadRetry.value: reading again fetches and decrypts the vault in place and enters it, landing at /dashboard in the same document, unlocked, with no password typed. Another failure draws the failure card again

heldKeysAreBound.value: the keys held while a new vault waits to be read are bound like an open vault's: the idle lock and the lock on pagehide discard them and draw the unlock card, which asks for the password only, with no username field

lockWinsOverRead.value: a lock during the first read or a later one wins. The read finishing opens nothing, draws nothing of the vault, and the unlock card stands

firstReadFailureCard.value: vault form only. The form gives way to a card of the same width announced as an alert, with the heading 'Your vault is created' and a primary 'Try again' button that disables itself while it reads again in place. Copy beyond those two strings is in the cited section

fixtures: a valid unused vault owner invite and a valid unused administrator invite
an invalid, an expired, a used and a revoked invite, for the byte-identical error assertion shared with admin-invites
request-payload capture over the whole registration flow, for the assertion that no password, Master Key or unwrapped DEK is sent

a hand-built POST /api/register carrying a kind field, a method field, a wrapper against an administrator invite, a missing wrapper against a vault owner invite, KDF parameters below the server minimum, and a salt that is not 16 bytes
a fault injected into the profile insert, for the all-or-nothing assertion including the unconsumed invite
a seeded account of each kind holding the same username, for the cross-kind collision refusal
an account registered through PUT /api/records with an equivalent profile record, for the indistinguishability assertion
another account's live session cookie, carried into a successful and into a failed registration
GET /api/records stubbed to answer 503 on the first read after a successful registration and switchable to answer normally on the retry, for the first-read-failure assertions
control of the idle timer and a way to fire pagehide, for the held-keys assertions, including a pagehide fired while the retried read is in flight
tests/fixtures/usernames.json, shared by pytest and the client tests
a hand-built POST /api/register with a username outside the rule, sent with a usable invite and with an unusable one, and one with a taken username and an unusable invite

POST /api/register stubbed to answer each of: refused invite, refused username, Conflict, Bad Request with no refused member, Bad Request with a non-JSON body, Content Too Large, Server Error, Service Unavailable, and a dropped connection
the derivation and the captured requests observable from the client test, for the assertion that a disabled button and Enter derive and send nothing
focus: the administrator path must leave zero dek_wrappers rows and zero records rows, asserted against both tables rather than against the response. Zero is the whole guarantee and an implementation that writes an empty wrapper row passes every behaviour test

the principals row must hold no salt, no KDF envelope, no Auth Key hash and no wrapped DEK, asserted against the table's full column set so the test fails if one is added back. Asserting the values are absent is not the same as asserting the columns are

the profile AAD must be shown to be built entirely before the request is sent, by encrypting the blob in a test with no server interaction at all. A test that checks the AAD after a successful registration cannot tell whether the client waited for an identity

a below-minimum KDF envelope must be rejected server-side even though the client UI would never send one. This is the case only a hand-built request reaches, and it is the one that decides whether the rule is a control or a convention
the request payload assertion has to run against the captured bytes, not against an inspection of the code, and it has to cover the password, the Master Key and the unwrapped DEK separately
the four bad-invite responses must be byte-identical, not merely similar in wording. Any difference in length, ordering or status turns the page into an oracle

the profile record written by registration must be indistinguishable from one written through PUT /api/records: same validation, same column values, same AAD. A second record writer that happens to produce the same columns today is exactly what this criterion exists to prevent
a registration that fails partway must leave the invite unconsumed, asserted against the invite row and not only against the absence of the account

a registration carrying another account's live cookie must delete that sessions row, asserted against the table, and the old cookie must answer Unauthorized. A failed registration must leave the carried session working

the first-read failure must be asserted as the same document: no navigation, no page load, no password field and no unlock card while the failure card shows, and the retry reaching /dashboard with no password typed. A test that reloads and signs in passes the outcome and breaks the rule

the held keys must be shown to be discarded by the idle period and by pagehide while the failure card shows, leaving the unlock card with a password field and no username field. A card that merely hides the keys passes a visual check and leaves them in memory

a pagehide while the retried read is in flight must leave no keys, no vault and nothing of the vault drawn, with the unlock card shown, asserted against the in-memory model and the DOM. A read that finishes after the lock and opens the vault anyway is the failure this catches

the order of the checks is only observable with two faults in one request: a taken username with an unusable invite must answer refused invite and not Conflict, and a username outside the rule must answer refused username whether the invite is usable or not. A test with one fault at a time passes any order
the five bad-token answers to POST /api/register must be byte-identical in status, headers and body, compared as raw bytes, as the four bad-invite pages from GET /register are

every Bad Request other than the two named reasons must be asserted to carry no refused member, by parsing the body. An implementation that tags every Bad Request with a reason passes every test that only checks status

the browser's check and the server's normalization must each be run over the whole shared fixture through the real code on both sides. A client test that re-implements the rule in the test passes while the two copies drift
a disabled button must be shown to block the derivation, not merely look disabled: press Enter in each field and assert against the derivation call and the captured requests

each stubbed answer must show its own message and no other, and every field, the password included, must keep its value in all but the invite's. Only Server Error, Service Unavailable and a dropped connection show the network wording
every refusal, Conflict included, must leave the invite pending and no principal row, asserted against both tables and not against the response

openQuestions: spec/features/register.md, Checks and their answers, does not place the blob-size cap (wrapped DEK and profile blobs, answered Content Too Large) in the check order. Step 3 names only base64 and length shape and step 7 the record validator, so the position of a wrapped DEK over its cap relative to the invite and taken checks is unstated.
